title: Curated Collection
description: Enriched research collection produced by Phase 1 (Curation). Items are deduplicated, filtered, and enriched with Claude-generated summaries, tags, and promoted metadata fields. This is the primary input for concept extraction and design synthesis. Schema is compatible with both cc_load_collection and synth_load_collection auto-detection.

collection_id.description: Same ID as the raw collection it was curated from

manifest_id.description: ID of the research manifest that produced the source raw collection

created_date.description: When the raw collection was originally created

metadata.description: Collection-level metadata (topic description, source info, limitations)

raw_count.description: Number of items in the raw collection before curation

filtered_out.description: Items removed by tag filters, content length, or quality assessment

final_count.description: Number of items in the curated collection

CuratedItem.description: Field names are chosen for compatibility with cc_load_collection and synth_load_collection auto-detection. Both servers detect: id, content, summary/title, tags, profile/author, date, url.

id.description: Unique item identifier (tweet_id, generated hash, etc.)

title.description: Short descriptive title (Claude-generated if not present in source)

summary.description: Claude-generated concise summary of the item's key information

author.description: Also detected as 'profile' by auto-detection (both field names work)

tags.description: Claude-assigned tags based on content analysis

strategy_type.description: Domain-specific: type of strategy (promoted from metadata by curation)

platform.description: Domain-specific: target platform (promoted from metadata by curation)

instrument.description: Domain-specific: financial instrument type (promoted from metadata by curation)

dependencies.description: Domain-specific: tools, APIs, or libraries referenced (promoted from metadata by curation)

metadata.description: All remaining fields not captured by primary or domain-specific fields
